message:
Lena, Farah, Kofi, sunlight can run the store from a shed-roof field using the fixed-tilt monocrystalline array (C1), where Photovoltaic (PV) means solar panels. Plain words, tropical sun gives a few peak hours so a few kilowatts cover about ten kilowatt-hour per day. Numbers are about 2.40 kilowatt peak from six 400 watt panels on about 12.0 square metres, sane against a parking space, per the peak-sun sizing rule (E1) and the 400 watt panel size of 1762 by 1134 millimetres (E4).

Night running needs stored charge beside the room in the battery plus controller cabinet (C2), where Lithium Iron Phosphate (LiFePO4) is the battery chemistry and Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) is solar charge control. Plain words, one night of cooling is about half a household day of energy. Numbers are 48 volt 100 ampere-hour holding 5.12 kilowatt-hour (E9) managed by a 60 ampere controller rated to 3200 watt at 48 volt (E10).

Losses stay low through the low-loss Direct Current wiring (C3), where Direct Current (DC) means panel-to-battery wires. Plain words, higher voltage halves current and heat loss. Numbers are series pairs over a few metres to hold drop to a few percent with fuses and disconnect. Not ready, because Lena's cooling load must confirm daily energy before sizes freeze.
